A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EFA research work. Their full main texts, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary materials are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original bias-mitigation and preservation experiments, ablations, and qualitative analyses on WinoBias and COCO-derived evaluations, including supplementary intersectional-bias results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds computational-efficiency measurements and complex-scene qualitative evaluations.

M1.justification: The attention predictor, reconstruction and regularization components, selected insertion layers, and attribute-sampling procedure are retained. Section 3.3 rewrites the existing regularizers using a common masked expression and exchanges coefficient labels; it does not establish a changed training procedure.

E1.justification: v2 Section 14 and Figure 7 add a targeted race-debiasing scenario involving multiple people, diverse objects, cultural contexts, and unclear faces. Existing training data, WinoBias prompts, COCO evaluations, and gender/race/age coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain Original SD, Concept Algebra, UCE, Finetuning Diffusion, and Interpret Diffusion. Concept Algebra+ already appears in v1's supplementary Tables 7–8; its presence in v2 is not a baseline addition.

E3.justification: New Section 11 evaluates parameter count and inference time for the existing gender/race/age EFA configuration against SD on an NVIDIA A100. Existing benchmark splits, image counts, metrics, and training schedules are retained; this is an additional evaluation rather than a documented revision of earlier experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds an efficiency analysis and a complex-scene case study that includes an unclear-face failure case. The regularization, segmentation-mask, and layer-resolution ablations, attention visualization, and Concept Algebra+ analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Matched-seed comparison practices remain unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and the added timing results introduce no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results in Tables 1–4 and 6–10 are unchanged. v2 newly reports SD versus EFA parameter counts of 1066M versus 1166M and inference times of 3.69 versus 3.98 seconds on an A100. It also adds complex-scene outcomes and replaces some Figure 1 examples; these are not demonstrated performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: The mask-parameterized regularizer and indexed attention-submatrix notation in v2 restate v1's existing mathematical operations. No substantive mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: identify attribute entanglement, introduce EFA for human-centric debiasing, and preserve non-target attributes and generative capacity while outperforming prior methods. The added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies unclear facial features as a failure condition for localizing and modifying racial cues. New Section 15 discusses the limitations of predefined bias types and human-centric coverage, while Section 11 discusses computational overhead and possible optimization.

D1.justification: Section 7 adds input-tensor dimensions and explains preservation of attention input/output shapes, while clarifying attribute-specific hyperparameter tuning. Section 11 supplies A100 hardware and computational-cost information. These extend documentation without establishing changes to the retained implementation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chinchure et al.'s TIBET reference and positions automatic bias identification as complementary to EFA in future work. Existing related-work coverage and the principal positioning against earlier debiasing approaches remain intact.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose revisions, clarifies counterfactual prompts and loss notation, and adds acknowledgments and supplementary efficiency and limitations sections. Most prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 refreshes and rearranges examples, Figures 2–3 revise notation, and new Figure 7 presents complex scenes. Table 9 moves between columns, and later supplementary figures are renumbered. Most existing visual material and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves practical assessability by quantifying previously unreported computational overhead, clarifying technical documentation, and adding explicit applicability limits and an illustrated failure case. The complex-scene evidence remains qualitative, and the method and existing benchmark results are unchanged, so these useful gains are incremental rather than a substantial strengthening of the paper.
